newsitem.title: JAPAN: Mitsui Toatsu polypropylene unit to join G.Polymer.
newsitem.headline: Mitsui Toatsu polypropylene unit to join G.Polymer.

text.p: Mitsui Toatsu Chemicals Inc said on Thursday it would merge its polypropylene unit into Grand Polymer Co Ltd, a venture including Mitsui's future merger partner, and take a one-third stake in the venture.

Mitsui Toatsu is set to merge in October with Mitsui Petrochemical Industries Ltd, which in 1995 joined with Ube Industries Ltd to create Grand Polymer by combining the two companies' polypropylene divisions.
"In this age of stiff international competition, it is imperative for Japan's petrochemical firms to pursue effectiveness through integration," a Mitsui Toatsu spokesman said.
Mitsui Toatsu will invest 2.5 billion yen in Grand Polymer in return for its one-third share, boosting the venture's total capital to 7.5 billion yen.

The merger with Mitsui Toatsu's polypropylene unit, scheduled for July 1, is expected to raise Grand Polymer's annual polypropylene capacity to 659,000 tonnes, or 23.5 percent of total domestic capacity.
That will make Grand Polymer Japan's second-largest producer, in terms of capacity, after Japan Polychem Corp, which has an annual capacity of 733,000 tonnes, or 26 percent of domestic capacity.
Japan Polychem is a joint venture between Tonen Chemical Corp and Mitsubishi Chemical Corp.
